caption: 400,000 men marched into Russia. Barely 10,000 came back.
text: Four-hundred-thousand men marched into Russia. Barely ten-thousand came back.

caption: June 1812. The biggest army Europe had ever seen crossed a river on the edge of the Russian Empire.
text: June eighteen-twelve. The biggest army Europe had ever seen crossed a river on the edge of the Russian Empire.

caption: Six months later, the survivors stumbled back across the same river. Ragged, frozen, a few hundred at a time.
text: Six months later, the survivors stumbled back across the same river. Ragged, frozen, a few hundred at a time.

caption: So here is today's question. Where did Europe's greatest army go? And no, it wasn't just the winter.
text: So here is today's question. Where did Europe's greatest army go? And no, it wasn't just the winter.

caption: Let's follow it on the map.
text: Let's follow it on the map.

caption: First, the man. In 1793, a 24-year-old artillery officer named Napoleon Bonaparte helped take the port of Toulon back from the British.
text: First, the man. In seventeen-ninety-three, a twenty-four-year-old artillery officer named Napoleon Bonaparte helped take the port of Toulon back from the British.

caption: Six years later he seized power in Paris. In 1804, he crowned himself Emperor of the French.
text: Six years later he seized power in Paris. In eighteen-oh-four, he crowned himself Emperor of the French.

caption: Then he beat almost everyone. Austria at Austerlitz. Prussia at Jena. Russia at Friedland.
text: Then he beat almost everyone. Austria at Austerlitz. Prussia at Jena. Russia at Friedland.

caption: By 1810, France ruled from Spain to the Baltic, and most of the rest of Europe was its ally or its puppet.
text: By eighteen-ten, France ruled from Spain to the Baltic, and most of the rest of Europe was its ally or its puppet.

caption: Quick quiz. Which of these did Napoleon never conquer? Austria, Prussia, or Britain?
text: Quick quiz. Which of these did Napoleon never conquer? Austria, Prussia, or Britain?

caption: Britain. Behind the Royal Navy, it was the one enemy he could not reach. And that is how Russia gets dragged into this story.
text: Britain. Behind the Royal Navy, it was the one enemy he could not reach. And that is how Russia gets dragged into this story.

caption: In 1806, Napoleon tried to beat Britain with money instead of guns. He banned all of Europe from trading with it.
text: In eighteen-oh-six, Napoleon tried to beat Britain with money instead of guns. He banned all of Europe from trading with it.

caption: In 1807, after his defeat at Friedland, Tsar Alexander the First made peace on a raft in the middle of a river, and agreed to join the ban.
text: In eighteen-oh-seven, after his defeat at Friedland, Tsar Alexander the First made peace on a raft in the middle of a river, and agreed to join the ban.

caption: But Russia lived on selling grain, timber and hemp to Britain. The ban was strangling its economy.
text: But Russia lived on selling grain, timber and hemp to Britain. The ban was strangling its economy.

caption: On the last day of 1810, Alexander opened his ports to neutral ships and slapped taxes on French goods. In practice, he had walked out.
text: On the last day of eighteen-ten, Alexander opened his ports to neutral ships and slapped taxes on French goods. In practice, he had walked out.

caption: And then there was Poland. Napoleon had built a Polish state right on Russia's border. The Tsar saw a knife at his throat.
text: And then there was Poland. Napoleon had built a Polish state right on Russia's border. The Tsar saw a knife at his throat.

caption: So Napoleon made his decision. March into Russia, win one big battle, and force the Tsar back into line. A short war.
text: So Napoleon made his decision. March into Russia, win one big battle, and force the Tsar back into line. A short war.

caption: To do it, he gathered the largest army Europe had ever assembled. The Grande Armée.
text: To do it, he gathered the largest army Europe had ever assembled. The Grande Armée.

caption: About 450,000 men in the first wave. Around 600,000 in all, once the reinforcements came up.
text: About four-hundred-fifty-thousand men in the first wave. Around six-hundred-thousand in all, once the reinforcements came up.

caption: Only about half of them were French. Poles, Germans, Italians, Austrians, Prussians, Swiss. A whole continent in one army.
text: Only about half of them were French. Poles, Germans, Italians, Austrians, Prussians, Swiss. A whole continent in one army.

caption: The Poles alone sent close to 100,000 men. They hoped Napoleon would give them back their country.
text: The Poles alone sent close to one-hundred-thousand men. They hoped Napoleon would give them back their country.

caption: It took up to 200,000 horses and about 1,300 cannon.
text: It took up to two-hundred-thousand horses and about one-thousand-three-hundred cannon.

caption: The problem was food. An army this size eats a mountain every day, and Russia's roads were dirt tracks.
text: The problem was food. An army this size eats a mountain every day, and Russia's roads were dirt tracks.

caption: Napoleon brought supplies for a few weeks. He was sure the war would be over by then.
text: Napoleon brought supplies for a few weeks. He was sure the war would be over by then.

caption: On the 24th of June 1812, the army crossed the Neman river at Kovno, today's Kaunas in Lithuania.
text: On the twenty-fourth of June eighteen-twelve, the army crossed the Neman river at Kovno, today's Kaunas in Lithuania.

caption: Now watch this line. Its width is the number of men. This is how a French engineer, Charles Minard, drew this campaign in 1869.
text: Now watch this line. Its width is the number of men. This is how a French engineer, Charles Minard, drew this campaign in eighteen-sixty-nine.

caption: Napoleon wanted a battle. The Russians refused to give him one. Their two armies kept pulling back, deeper and deeper.
text: Napoleon wanted a battle. The Russians refused to give him one. Their two armies kept pulling back, deeper and deeper.

caption: Four days after crossing, he took Vilna without a fight. The Russians had already left.
text: Four days after crossing, he took Vilna without a fight. The Russians had already left.

caption: As they went, they burned crops, villages, and anything the French could eat.
text: As they went, they burned crops, villages, and anything the French could eat.

caption: Then came the weather. Summer storms that turned roads to mud, then scorching heat, dust, and bad water.
text: Then came the weather. Summer storms that turned roads to mud, then scorching heat, dust, and bad water.

caption: Typhus and dysentery spread through the ranks. Horses died by the thousands in the first weeks.
text: Typhus and dysentery spread through the ranks. Horses died by the thousands in the first weeks.

caption: Men deserted, fell behind, or simply dropped. In the first month alone, about 100,000 were gone.
text: Men deserted, fell behind, or simply dropped. In the first month alone, about one-hundred-thousand were gone.

caption: At Vitebsk, in late July, Napoleon stopped for two weeks, hoping the Russians would finally come and fight. They never did.
text: At Vitebsk, in late July, Napoleon stopped for two weeks, hoping the Russians would finally come and fight. They never did.

caption: Look at the line. It's already a third thinner, and the real fighting hasn't even started.
text: Look at the line. It's already a third thinner, and the real fighting hasn't even started.

caption: In mid-August, at Smolensk, the French finally caught the Russians. The city burned, and the Russians slipped away again.
text: In mid-August, at Smolensk, the French finally caught the Russians. The city burned, and the Russians slipped away again.

caption: In three days of fighting, around 10,000 French and 12,000 Russians were killed or wounded.
text: In three days of fighting, around ten-thousand French and twelve-thousand Russians were killed or wounded.

caption: Napoleon had a choice. Stop for the winter, or push on to Moscow. He pushed on.
text: Napoleon had a choice. Stop for the winter, or push on to Moscow. He pushed on.

caption: In Russia, people were furious about the endless retreat. The Tsar gave command to an old, one-eyed general. Mikhail Kutuzov.
text: In Russia, people were furious about the endless retreat. The Tsar gave command to an old, one-eyed general. Mikhail Kutuzov.

caption: And Kutuzov finally turned to fight. At a village called Borodino, about 120 kilometres west of Moscow.
text: And Kutuzov finally turned to fight. At a village called Borodino, about one-hundred-twenty kilometres west of Moscow.

caption: The 7th of September 1812. About 130,000 French and allies, against more than 120,000 Russians, and over 1,200 cannon between them.
text: The seventh of September eighteen-twelve. About one-hundred-thirty-thousand French and allies, against more than one-hundred-twenty-thousand Russians, and over one-thousand-two-hundred cannon between them.

caption: They fought from dawn until dark, over Russian earthworks: the flèches, and the Great Redoubt.
text: They fought from dawn until dark, over Russian earthworks: the flèches, and the Great Redoubt.

caption: By nightfall, more than 70,000 men were dead or wounded. The bloodiest single day of the Napoleonic Wars.
text: By nightfall, more than seventy-thousand men were dead or wounded. The bloodiest single day of the Napoleonic Wars.

caption: Napoleon refused to send in his Imperial Guard, his last reserve. The Russian army survived, and pulled back in order.
text: Napoleon refused to send in his Imperial Guard, his last reserve. The Russian army survived, and pulled back in order.

caption: The French held the field. But it was not the knockout blow Napoleon needed.
text: The French held the field. But it was not the knockout blow Napoleon needed.

caption: Quiz time. After Borodino, what did Kutuzov do? Attack again, defend Moscow, or give Moscow up?
text: Quiz time. After Borodino, what did Kutuzov do? Attack again, defend Moscow, or give Moscow up?

caption: He gave it up. Without a fight. To save its army, Russia abandoned its ancient capital.
text: He gave it up. Without a fight. To save its army, Russia abandoned its ancient capital.

caption: On the 14th of September, Napoleon reached Moscow. He waited for the city's leaders to bring him the keys. Nobody came.
text: On the fourteenth of September, Napoleon reached Moscow. He waited for the city's leaders to bring him the keys. Nobody came.

caption: Of a city of 270,000 people, almost everyone had left.
text: Of a city of two-hundred-seventy-thousand people, almost everyone had left.

caption: That night, fires broke out. For four days Moscow burned. About three quarters of the city was destroyed.
text: That night, fires broke out. For four days Moscow burned. About three quarters of the city was destroyed.

caption: Who started it? Most historians blame the Russians themselves, probably on the orders of the governor, Rostopchin. It's still debated.
text: Who started it? Most historians blame the Russians themselves, probably on the orders of the governor, Rostopchin. It's still debated.

caption: Napoleon sat in the Kremlin and wrote to the Tsar, offering peace. Alexander never answered.
text: Napoleon sat in the Kremlin and wrote to the Tsar, offering peace. Alexander never answered.

caption: For five weeks the Emperor waited in a burned city, as autumn turned cold. His army looted, drank, and fell apart.
text: For five weeks the Emperor waited in a burned city, as autumn turned cold. His army looted, drank, and fell apart.

caption: On the 18th of October, Kutuzov struck a French outpost south of Moscow, at Tarutino. Napoleon finally understood. There would be no peace.
text: On the eighteenth of October, Kutuzov struck a French outpost south of Moscow, at Tarutino. Napoleon finally understood. There would be no peace.

caption: On the 19th of October, he finally ordered the retreat. About 100,000 men marched out, dragging carts full of loot.
text: On the nineteenth of October, he finally ordered the retreat. About one-hundred-thousand men marched out, dragging carts full of loot.

caption: Behind them, on Napoleon's orders, the rearguard blew up parts of the Kremlin.
card: Blown up on the way out
text: Behind them, on Napoleon's orders, the rearguard blew up parts of the Kremlin.

caption: He tried to go home by a new road, south, through untouched farmland. At Maloyaroslavets, the Russians blocked the way.
text: He tried to go home by a new road, south, through untouched farmland. At Maloyaroslavets, the Russians blocked the way.

caption: So the army turned back onto the road it came in on. The road it had already stripped bare.
text: So the army turned back onto the road it came in on. The road it had already stripped bare.

caption: At Vyazma, on the 3rd of November, Russian troops caught the rearguard and mauled it. The retreat became a running fight.
text: At Vyazma, on the third of November, Russian troops caught the rearguard and mauled it. The retreat became a running fight.

caption: In early November, real winter arrived. On Minard's map, a second line appears at the bottom. The temperature.
text: In early November, real winter arrived. On Minard's map, a second line appears at the bottom. The temperature.

caption: The last horses died. Cannon and wagons were left in the snow. Without cavalry, nobody could scout or guard the column.
text: The last horses died. Cannon and wagons were left in the snow. Without cavalry, nobody could scout or guard the column.

caption: Cossacks rode out of the forests, cut down stragglers, and vanished. Anyone who fell behind was lost.
text: Cossacks rode out of the forests, cut down stragglers, and vanished. Anyone who fell behind was lost.

caption: Men burned wagons for warmth and ate the horses that fell. By early December, nights dropped below minus 30 degrees.
text: Men burned wagons for warmth and ate the horses that fell. By early December, nights dropped below minus thirty degrees.

caption: On the 9th of November, the army staggered back into Smolensk. Only about 60,000 men were still fit to fight.
text: On the ninth of November, the army staggered back into Smolensk. Only about sixty-thousand men were still fit to fight.

caption: At Krasnoi, in mid-November, the Russians struck again. Marshal Ney's rearguard was almost wiped out.
text: At Krasnoi, in mid-November, the Russians struck again. Marshal Ney's rearguard was almost wiped out.

caption: Then came the Berezina river. The bridge had been burned, and Russian armies were closing in from three sides.
text: Then came the Berezina river. The bridge had been burned, and Russian armies were closing in from three sides.

caption: French engineers under General Eblé stood in the freezing water for hours and built two bridges. Few of them lived to see the spring.
text: French engineers under General Eblé stood in the freezing water for hours and built two bridges. Few of them lived to see the spring.

caption: For three days the army crossed. On the last morning the bridges were burned, and thousands of stragglers were left on the far bank.
text: For three days the army crossed. On the last morning the bridges were burned, and thousands of stragglers were left on the far bank.

caption: On the 5th of December, Napoleon left his army and raced back to Paris in a sledge.
text: On the fifth of December, Napoleon left his army and raced back to Paris in a sledge.

caption: In mid-December, the last of the main army crossed the Neman again. On Minard's map, a band of 422,000 men ends at 10,000.
text: In mid-December, the last of the main army crossed the Neman again. On Minard's map, a band of four-hundred-twenty-two-thousand men ends at ten-thousand.

caption: Counting the corps on the flanks, maybe 100,000 got out in all. But the Grande Armée was gone.
text: Counting the corps on the flanks, maybe one-hundred-thousand got out in all. But the Grande Armée was gone.

caption: So, where did Europe's greatest army go?
text: So, where did Europe's greatest army go?

caption: Mostly not to the winter. Look at the line. Most of it had already vanished before the first snow fell.
text: Mostly not to the winter. Look at the line. Most of it had already vanished before the first snow fell.

caption: It was distance. Supply. Disease. Heat. A Russian army that refused to fight on Napoleon's terms, and a country willing to burn its own land.
text: It was distance. Supply. Disease. Heat. A Russian army that refused to fight on Napoleon's terms, and a country willing to burn its own land.

caption: Russia paid a terrible price too. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians died.
text: Russia paid a terrible price too. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians died.

caption: On the French side, around 100,000 men were taken prisoner.
text: On the French side, around one-hundred-thousand men were taken prisoner.

caption: Within weeks, his allies began to turn. On the 30th of December, the Prussian corps in his army made its own deal with the Russians.
text: Within weeks, his allies began to turn. On the thirtieth of December, the Prussian corps in his army made its own deal with the Russians.

caption: In October 1813, at Leipzig, more than half a million soldiers met in the largest battle of the Napoleonic Wars. Napoleon lost.
text: In October eighteen-thirteen, at Leipzig, more than half a million soldiers met in the largest battle of the Napoleonic Wars. Napoleon lost.

caption: For Napoleon, it was the beginning of the end. In less than two years, his enemies were in Paris, and he was in exile on Elba.
text: For Napoleon, it was the beginning of the end. In less than two years, his enemies were in Paris, and he was in exile on Elba.

caption: And the best picture of this disaster was drawn 57 years later, by a retired French engineer. Some call it the best statistical graphic ever made.
text: And the best picture of this disaster was drawn fifty-seven years later, by a retired French engineer. Some call it the best statistical graphic ever made.

caption: Now, your turn. If you were Napoleon, when would you have turned back? Tell me in the comments.
text: Now, your turn. If you were Napoleon, when would you have turned back? Tell me in the comments.
